beats.lead: The iPhone and the App Store feel inseparable now
beats.text: For its first thirteen months, there was no App Store at all.
beats.note: Steve Jobs's actual plan was that there never would be. At WWDC in 2007 he told developers to build web apps for Safari instead: 'There's no SDK that you need!'

beats.name: Art Levinson
beats.role: An Apple board member who, according to Walter Isaacson's biography of Jobs, phoned him 'half a dozen times' to lobby for native third-party apps. Jobs kept shutting the conversation down.

beats.lead: He changed his mind in an open letter
beats.note: Jobs announced a real software development kit was coming the following March. It shipped on schedule, on 6 March 2008.

beats.context: Native apps already live when the App Store opened on 10 July 2008, more than a year after the iPhone itself went on sale. Jobs called it 'the biggest launch of my career.'

beats.text: It took a board member phoning him again and again to change his mind.

beats.line: The thing that made the iPhone the iPhone almost didn't happen at all.
